title: The Prophet's intercession
hookLine: the Prophet ﷺ will intercede for his community (Bukhari)

cards: The plain is crowded and the waiting is long, and people do what people do when things are hard: they look for someone to speak for them. A hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, narrated by Anas, tells it as a search.
They go to Adam: will you ask your Lord for us? Not me, he says, and sends them on. To Noah.
Not me. To Abraham. To Moses.
To Jesus. Each one gently says: not me, go to another. And the last one sends them to the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.

teach.b: The word is shafa'ah, intercession: speaking to someone on another's behalf. In the hadith, the Prophet goes, and the first thing he does is not speak. He falls down in prostration before his Lord, and stays there.
Then he is told: raise your head; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and your intercession will be accepted. Then he intercedes. Two things hold this teaching in place.
First, the Qur'an is clear that intercession is never a way around Allah.

In the Throne Verse, Pickthall's translation asks: "Who is he that intercedeth with Him save by His leave?" Nobody speaks on the Day unless permitted; the Prophet's intercession is a permission, granted.

teach.h: ONE PRAYER, KEPT FOR THE DAY.
teach.b: Another hadith in Bukhari has him say that every prophet has one prayer sure to be answered, and he wanted to keep his back, as intercession for his community on the Day of Resurrection.

Theologians from the part we just finished discussed who it reaches. Sunni theologians, as they're remembered, affirmed that it can reach believers who sinned gravely; the Mu'tazilah held a narrower view.
The hadith also name a way to ask for it.

A hadith in Sahih Muslim says that whoever sends one blessing on the Prophet, Allah sends ten on them; and that whoever, after the call to prayer, asks Allah to grant him the station called al-wasilah, his intercession becomes due for that person.
So the blessing travels both ways: the community sends salawat to him, and the hope is that he speaks for them.

how: Muslims send blessings on the Prophet, salawat, in their prayers and when his name is mentioned, and after the call to prayer they may ask Allah to grant him al-wasilah, hoping for his intercession on the Day of Resurrection.

o: the prostration made in prayer before asking for a need
intercession: speaking for another, only by Allah's leave
a blessing sent on the Prophet after the call to prayer

games.q: the Prophet's intercession — tap the pairs.
p: asked for him after the call to prayer

s: in the Qur'an, intercession can happen without Allah's leave
the Throne Verse: "Who is he that intercedeth with Him save by His leave?"
in the hadith, the Prophet's first act on the Day is to prostrate
then he is told: raise your head; intercede, and it will be accepted.
by a hadith in Bukhari, the Prophet used his sure prayer during his lifetime
he kept it back as intercession for his community on the Day.

games.q: you're the Prophet, and the people have come to you after every other prophet said 'not me.' what do you do first?
o: fall down in prostration before your Lord.
games.why: he prostrates first, and is told: raise your head; ask, and you will be given; intercede, and it will be accepted.

practice: If you're Muslim, say the familiar words slowly, a few times, in Arabic or in English: allahumma salli 'ala Muhammad, O Allah, send blessings on Muhammad.

If you're not, sit with the shape of the idea: bring to mind someone who once spoke up for you when you couldn't speak for yourself, a parent, a teacher, a friend in a hard meeting, and wish them well.

wordCard.voice: Shafa'ah. Intercession: speaking for another, only by Allah's leave; the Prophet's, Muslims hold, kept for his community on the Day. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: intercession, speaking on another's behalf.

carryVoice: Your line: he will intercede. Only by Allah's leave, and kept for the Day. Rest easy tonight.
